title: review-route input
description:
Input envelope consumed by `plan_ops.py review-route`. Encodes the parsed Phase D review state for one task: who implemented, who reviewed, the runtime mode, the reviewer envelope, the optional D.5 third-opinion envelope, retry budget consumed so far on this task, and routing flags. The subcommand maps this to one routing directive — see review_route_output_schema.json.

Compatibility window (TASK-001 PHASE_D_STATE_MACHINE_COMPLETION): the canonical fields are `task_id`, `implementer`, `reviewer`, `claude_only`, `reviewer_envelope`, `d5_envelope`, `retries_used`, and `flags`. For one release window, payloads that omit the new `reviewer` and `claude_only` fields remain accepted; the router infers `reviewer` from `implementer` (claude→codex, codex→claude) and defaults `claude_only=false`. After the compatibility window, callers SHOULD always send the canonical fields explicitly.

task_id.description: Three-digit task id (`NNN` or `NNN<A-Z>`). Round-tripped into the directive so dispatch templates have it.

implementer.description: Which implementer produced the work under review. Drives D.2 / D.2a vs D.2b dispatch (Claude-impl → Codex/Gemini-review escalates via D.5 unless `claude_only=true`; Codex-impl → Claude-review escalates via role-swap).

reviewer.description: Reviewer identity. Canonical TASK-001 field — first-class so the router does not have to infer reviewer semantics from the implementer alone. `codex` and `gemini` share the Codex verdict vocabulary on Claude work; `gemini` can also review Codex work in the Codex+Gemini no-Claude path. `claude` paired with Claude implementer requires `claude_only=true`. `none` is the explicit skip-review path: the router emits `commit` with reviewer metadata suitable for `commit-task reviewer=none`. Optional during the compatibility window — see top-level description.

claude_only.description: Runtime mode flag bound at Phase 0 preflight (`--claude-only OR codex_available=false`). When `true`, Codex/Gemini shell-out is forbidden, the D.5 / D.2a.5 / D.2a.6 ladder collapses, and a Claude-reviewer `needs-rework` on Claude work routes straight to D.4 (action `fail`). Optional during the compatibility window — see top-level description.

unattended_revert_policy.description: Policy decision bound from `$UNATTENDED_REVERT_POLICY`. In codex-review-binding mode, `pause` routes reviewer `needs-rework` to `pause_awaiting_user` with stage `post_binding_block`; `fail-fast` and `preserve-only` route to `fail` with machine-readable authorization metadata.

reviewer_envelope.description: Parsed review envelope. `verdict` vocabulary depends on reviewer: Codex reviewer emits `clean|minor-findings|needs-rework`; Claude reviewer emits `ship|ship-with-fixes|needs-rework`.

d5_envelope.description: Phase D.5 third-opinion envelope when D.2a fired; `null` when no D.5 dispatch happened. `verdict` is one of `ship|ship-with-fixes|partial-agreement|needs-rework`. `load_bearing` and `dismissed` carry the index split for the `partial-agreement` path.

retries_used.description: Per-task retry budget consumed prior to this routing call. Each is one-shot; `true` means the budget is exhausted.

flags.description: Routing-affecting flags surfaced from CLI / SKILL state.

codex_review_binding.description: When `true` and reviewer is Codex on Claude work with `needs-rework`, route straight to `fail` — no D.5, no remediation.

skip_cross_review.description: Reserved; reviewer envelope still drives routing in v1.
